Calculate Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI)

Source: R/calc_indices.R
calc_evi.Rd

Computes the Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), optimizing the vegetation signal with improved sensitivity in high biomass regions and reduced atmospheric aerosol influences.

Usage

calc_evi(nir, red, blue, G = 2.5, C1 = 6, C2 = 7.5, L = 1)

Arguments

nir

Near-infrared band (terra::SpatRaster or numeric).

red

Red band (terra::SpatRaster or numeric).

blue

Blue band (terra::SpatRaster or numeric).

G

Gain factor. Defaults to 2.5.

C1

Atmospheric resistance coefficient for red. Defaults to 6.0.

C2

Atmospheric resistance coefficient for blue. Defaults to 7.5.

L

Canopy background adjustment. Defaults to 1.0.

Value

A terra::SpatRaster (named "EVI") or numeric vector with index values.

Details

$$EVI = G \times \frac{NIR - RED}{NIR + C1 \times RED - C2 \times BLUE + L}$$

Description & Purpose: EVI was developed to enhance the vegetation signal in dense canopies where NDVI saturates, while reducing canopy background noise and aerosol scattering using the blue band.

Important - Reflectance Scale: EVI constants (G = 2.5, C1 = 6.0, C2 = 7.5, L = 1.0) were calibrated for physical surface reflectance in [0, 1]. If your input data are stored in raw integer Digital Numbers (e.g., Sentinel-2 L2A [0, 10000]), divide the inputs by 10000 or use geo_index(..., scale_factor = 10000).

References

Liu, H. Q., & Huete, A. (1995). A feedback based modification of the NDVI to minimize canopy background and atmospheric noise. IEEE TGRS, 33(2), 457-465.

See also

geo_index, calc_ndvi, calc_savi

Examples

# Numeric example with surface reflectance values in [0, 1]
calc_evi(nir = 0.50, red = 0.20, blue = 0.10)
#> [1] 0.3846154

# Raster example
img <- get_example_data()
evi_rast <- calc_evi(nir = img[["nir"]], red = img[["red"]], blue = img[["blue"]])
print(evi_rast)
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 10, 10, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 10, 10  (x, y)
#> extent      : 440000, 440100, 5410000, 5410100  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : WGS 84 / UTM zone 31N (EPSG:32631)
#> source(s)   : memory
#> name        :       EVI
#> min value   : -0.114944
#> max value   :  1.138812
